00070| /// The next deterministic step the server takes in an agentic coding loop.
00071| #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
00072| pub enum AgenticPlan {

00074|     ToolCalls(Vec<PlannedToolCall>),
00075|     /// The task is complete; this is the final assistant answer.
00076|     Final(String),
00077| }

00079| /// A single tool call the planner wants the server to emit.

00082|     /// The tool name to invoke (taken verbatim from the request's tools).
00083|     pub tool: String,
00084|     /// JSON-encoded arguments object for the call.

00088| /// The tool capabilities the planner's recipe relies on.
00089| ///
00090| /// This is the single source of truth for "what kind of thing a tool does". Both
00091| /// the planner (to pick which advertised tool to call for each recipe step) and
00092| /// the server's permission gate (to decide whether an agentic client may drive a
00093| /// tool of this kind) classify tool names through [`tool_capability`] — so the
00094| /// two never drift and no per-tool-name special cases accumulate.
00095| #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
00096| pub enum Capability {

00098|     Fetch,
00099|     Read,
00100|     Write,
00101|     Edit,
00102|     Run,
00103|     Grep,
00104|     Glob,
00105|     ListDir,
00106|     Todo,
00107|     Subagent,
00108|     ReadMany,
00109|     MultiEdit,
00110|     AskUser,
00111| }

00117|     /// (`write`, `write_file`, `edit`, `patch`, …) maps to the same permission.
00118|     #[must_use]
00119|     pub const fn permission_key(self) -> &'static str {

00168| /// Plan the next agentic step from the conversation and advertised tools.
00169| /// Returns [`None`] when neither a stored recipe nor a safe general plan applies.
00170| #[must_use]
00171| pub fn plan_chat_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str]) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {
00172|     let received = crate::protocol::latest_user_request(messages)?;
00173|     // A harness prompt that quotes the task to have it summarized is answered
00174|     // with the summary, never by doing the task again (issue #1133).
00175|     if let Some(summary) = harness_envelope::summarize_request(&received) {
00176|         return Some(AgenticPlan::Final(summary));
00177|     }
00178|     // A restart over prepared work (changed paths plus a pull request link)
00179|     // is the whole turn's shape, not one arm of the precedence cascade: it is
00180|     // decided on the same effective request the cascade reads, ahead of it,
00181|     // and its plan still passes the repeated-call and repeated-failure stops.
00182|     let effective = continued_agent_task(messages, &received);
00183|     let restart = super::restart_feedback::plan_restart(
00184|         effective.as_deref().unwrap_or(&received),
00185|         messages,
00186|         tool_names,
00187|     );
00188|     let plan = restart.or_else(|| plan_chat_step_routes(messages, tool_names, received))?;
00189|     Some(stop_repeated_failure(
00190|         stop_repeated_call(plan, messages),
00191|         messages,
00192|     ))
00193| }

00195| /// A tool call this turn already completed is not a plan again (issue #1154).
00196| ///
00197| /// Independent of any argument parsing: whatever keys a client names its
00198| /// arguments by, a stateless planner that re-derives a call whose result is
00199| /// already in the transcript ignored that result. The Codex Rust run planned
00200| /// the identical `gh issue view` 78 times over 6.2M input tokens because the
00201| /// read's accounting could not see the `cmd` key; this stop would have ended
00202| /// the loop on the second attempt whatever the parser did. The repeat is
00203| /// answered by reporting the stuck step and its last result.
00204| fn stop_repeated_call(plan: AgenticPlan, messages: &[ChatMessage]) -> AgenticPlan {
00205|     let AgenticPlan::ToolCalls(calls) = &plan else {
00206|         return plan;
00207|     };
00208|     let progress = Progress::scan(messages);
00209|     let Some((repeated, attempt)) = calls
00210|         .iter()
00211|         .find_map(|call| progress.repeated_call(call).map(|attempt| (call, attempt)))
00212|     else {
00213|         return plan;
00214|     };
00215|     AgenticPlan::Final(super::work_item_steps::fill(
00216|         "stuck_step_report",
00217|         &[
00218|             (
00219|                 "{step}",
00220|                 &format!("{} {}", repeated.tool, repeated.arguments),
00221|             ),
00222|             ("{result}", attempt.detail.trim()),
00223|         ],
00224|     ))
00225| }
00226| 
00227| /// A tool call that has already failed twice this turn with the same report
00228| /// is not a plan; the third attempt is replaced by the report of the failure.
00229| ///
00230| /// Issue #1133: the Kotlin run planned `mcp__playwright__browser_click` 547
00231| /// times, each answered by the same selector error, until the context window
00232| /// overflowed. No route knows it is looping -- each re-derives the same next
00233| /// step from the same transcript -- so the stop is applied to whatever any
00234| /// route planned.
00235| fn stop_repeated_failure(plan: AgenticPlan, messages: &[ChatMessage]) -> AgenticPlan {
00236|     const REPEATED_FAILURES_THAT_STOP: usize = 2;
00237|     let AgenticPlan::ToolCalls(calls) = &plan else {
00238|         return plan;
00239|     };
00240|     let progress = Progress::scan(messages);
00241|     let Some(repeated) = calls
00242|         .iter()
00243|         .find(|call| progress.identical_failures_of(&call.tool) >= REPEATED_FAILURES_THAT_STOP)
00244|     else {
00245|         return plan;
00246|     };
00247|     let Some(failure) = progress.latest_failure_of_tool(&repeated.tool) else {
00248|         return plan;
00249|     };
00250|     let prompt = crate::protocol::latest_user_request(messages).unwrap_or_default();
00251|     AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render_failure(
00252|         &repeated.tool,
00253|         &failure.detail,
00254|         &prompt,
00255|     ))
00256| }

00258| fn plan_chat_step_routes(
00259|     messages: &[ChatMessage],
00260|     tool_names: &[&str],
00261|     received: String,
00262| ) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {
00263|     // Load-time precedence join (plan 10 leaf 18): first plan step of a run
00264|     // proves the seed still names the cascade this function is about to walk.
00265|     checked_route_precedence();
00266|     trace_route("agentic_received", &received);
00267|     // Agent compacts a long tool loop by asking the model to summarize it, then
00268|     // starts the next request with the protocol turn "Continue if you have next
00269|     // steps". The work is still present, but only inside the assistant's
00270|     // `Conversation summary:` envelope. Treating the protocol turn as a fresh
00271|     // request loses that work and sends the sentence itself to web search.
00272|     // Recover only our own summary envelope, immediately before the exact
00273|     // continuation turn; ordinary user requests that happen to say "continue"
00274|     // keep their normal meaning.
00275|     let effective = continued_agent_task(messages, &received).unwrap_or(received);
00276|     // An *unmarked* harness preamble is still the caller talking (issue #907,
00277|     // follow-up). `<session_context>`-style markup is stripped upstream in
00278|     // `crate::protocol`, but Hive Mind's adapters concatenated their workflow
00279|     // policy and the objective into one untagged user message, so the tell has
00280|     // to be the objective delimiter the caller wrote instead of a tag:
00281|     // everything before a line-anchored `Issue to solve:` / `Task:` / `Goal:`
00282|     // lead is the caller's framing, and only the text after it is the request.
00283|     //
00284|     // Routing the whole message let the preamble win: "When running sudo
00285|     // commands, run them in the background." paired a run verb with the `sudo`
00286|     // shell token and planned bare `sudo`, and "Your prepared working
00287|     // directory: …" planned `pwd`, in both cases dropping the repository work
00288|     // that followed. The general planner already read the objective this way
00289|     // (issue #904); every other route now reads it the same way, so one
00290|     // boundary serves the whole router rather than one recipe.
00291|     let task = objective_text(&effective).to_owned();
00292|     trace_route("agentic_task", &task);
00293|     // A bare continuation cue with nothing to resume is still the cue here,
00294|     // and the `agentic_continuation` conversation handler answers it; the
00295|     // words of the cue are never a request (issue #1095).
00296|     if crate::rule_interpreter::handler_matches("conversation_control", &task)
00297|         || is_continuation_cue(&task)
00298|         // An edit request's block is its payload: a `when … then` inside it is
00299|         // text being written, not a skill being taught (PR #1188 T57).
00300|         || (!has_authoritative_literal_write(&task)
00301|             && super::general_planner::compose_edit_request(&task).is_none()
00302|             && looks_like_skill_description(super::positional_edit::own_text(&task)))
00303|     {
00304|         return None;
00305|     }
00306|     // Issue #707: seed-defined computer-use plans own their exact multilingual
00307|     // prompts before broad write/search routing. Each emitted primitive carries
00308|     // explicit pre/postconditions and is executed by the advertising client.
00309|     // Ahead of them, quotes that do not pair leave no telling the quoted text
00310|     // from the instruction, so the request is declined before any arm reads its
00311|     // payload as words to act on (PR #1188 G71).
00312|     if let Some(plan) = super::quote_nesting::request_fault_answer(
00313|         &task,
00314|         tool_for(tool_names, Capability::MultiEdit).is_some(),
00315|     )
00316|     .or_else(|| crate::computer_use::plan_agentic_step(messages, tool_names))
00317|     {
00318|         return Some(plan);
00319|     }
00320|     // An explicit exact-content marker makes the following bytes authoritative.
00321|     // Claim this narrow shape before edit/source semantics inspect the payload:
00322|     // literal bytes may themselves say "rename X to Y" (issue #708). Broader
00323|     // file-write requests remain below the semantic coding routes.
00324|     if has_authoritative_literal_write(&task)
00325|         && let Some(plan) = capability_router::workspace_creation_tool(tool_names)
00326|             .and_then(|_| compose_general_change_plan(&task))
00327|             .map(|plan| plan_general_change_step(messages, tool_names, &plan))
00328|     {
00329|         return Some(plan);
00330|     }
00331|     // Bind a program's semantic operands before treating its source path as a
00332|     // destination for a report about the rest of the request.
00333|     if let Some(mut answer) =
00334|         crate::coding::program_contract::answer(&task, &mut crate::event_log::EventLog::default())
00335|     {
00336|         if let Some(recipe) = answer.execution_recipe.as_mut()
00337|             && super::ci_workflow::requested_in(&task)
00338|         {
00339|             super::ci_workflow::attach(recipe);
00340|         }
00341|         if let Some(plan) =
00342|             super::command_reroute::plan_symbolic_command_reroute(messages, tool_names, &answer)
00343|         {
00344|             return Some(plan);
00345|         }
00346|     }
00347|     // "Find this out and leave the answer in FILE" (issue #1066). This sits ahead
00348|     // of every route that reads a request's lone file-shaped token, because that
00349|     // token is the *destination* here and opening it for reading ends the run with
00350|     // the evidence file unwritten. It sits behind the literal-write routes above,
00351|     // which own a request that spells its bytes out; this one owns the request
00352|     // whose bytes still have to be found.
00353|     //
00354|     // It sits ahead of the change routes below for the same reason it sits ahead
00355|     // of the readers: a request can carry both halves. The ladder's leaf says
00356|     // "Edit `src/engine_responses.rs` … Then create `agent-ladder-effects/…lino`
00357|     // recording what you changed. Leave evidence in `.agent-ladder/…-proof.md`",
00358|     // and the change routes answer `Final` for the whole request the moment the
00359|     // edit lands, so the two records the caller verifies are never written and
00360|     // the node fails `missing_proof` having done the work. This route peels one
00361|     // delivery at a time and re-plans the residual (see `parse_obligation`), so
00362|     // the change route still receives the edit -- with only the edit left in it.
00363|     if let Some(plan) = evidence_record::plan_evidence_record_step(&task, messages, tool_names) {
00364|         return Some(plan);
00365|     }
00366|     plan_settled_routes(&task, messages, tool_names)
00367| }

00369| /// Every route below the delivery peeling above, as one function.
00370| ///
00371| /// [`plan_evidence_record_step`](evidence_record::plan_evidence_record_step)
00372| /// peels a named destination off a request and re-plans the remainder, and that
00373| /// is only ever the right reading when the destination is not already some
00374| /// other route's whole answer. A registered recipe *is* named by its artifact —
00375| /// `learning_report::route` matches a prompt precisely by finding its own
00376| /// `path` in it — so peeling that path off leaves a residual that no longer
00377| /// reaches the recipe, and the request is answered by whatever the remainder
00378| /// happens to look like instead.
00379| ///
00380| /// Splitting the tail out lets the peeling ask the question directly: plan the
00381| /// *whole* request through the routes below and see whether one of them writes
00382| /// the file. Nothing here re-enters the peeling, so asking cannot recurse.
00383| pub(super) fn plan_settled_routes(
00384|     task: &str,
00385|     messages: &[ChatMessage],
00386|     tool_names: &[&str],
00387| ) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {
00388|     // A request to commit what is already in the tree is one shell step. It
00389|     // is claimed first because its words ("review these changes and commit
00390|     // them", with a `?? Main.scala` listing) read to later routes as a search
00391|     // for the file; the route itself declines any request that also names the
00392|     // work to do (issue #1133).
00393|     if let Some(plan) = git_commit::plan_commit_step(task, messages, tool_names) {
00394|         return Some(plan);
00395|     }
00396|     // A learned workspace-change procedure owns grounded repository rewrites
00397|     // and multi-file compositions before source creation or shell routing can
00398|     // collapse them into one incomplete action. A function and its test added
00399|     // to existing modules (PR #1188 T1) is one such composition: read both
00400|     // modules, write both, run the stated command.
00401|     // A copy or move followed by edits of the file it makes is planned
00402|     // sentence by sentence (PR #1188 G82).
00403|     if let Some(plan) = super::request_sequence::plan_request_sequence_step(
00404|         task,
00405|         messages,
00406|         tool_names,
00407|         plan_chat_step,
00408|     )
00409|     .or_else(|| super::workspace_change::plan_workspace_change_step(task, messages, tool_names))
00410|     .or_else(|| super::module_function::plan_module_function_step(task, messages, tool_names))
00411|     // A bug report with a stated expectation is checked before anything is
00412|     // rewritten (PR #1188 T93).
00413|     .or_else(|| {
00414|         super::function_expectation::plan_function_expectation_step(task, messages, tool_names)
00415|     })
00416|     // An assertion of a stated call and value is added in the test
00417|     // file's own form, and the file is run (PR #1188 G13).
00418|     .or_else(|| super::test_assertion::plan_test_assertion_step(task, messages, tool_names))
00419|     // A test asked for with no expected result is a question (PR #1188
00420|     // G25).
00421|     .or_else(|| super::function_expectation::test_expectation_question(task))
00422|     {
00423|         return Some(plan);
00424|     }
00425|     // A source-code description is not literal file content. Lower bounded
00426|     // seed-backed source tasks before the broad literal-write parser so coding
00427|     // requests produce executable bytes and verify those exact bytes.
00428|     if let Some(plan) = code_task::plan_generated_source_step(task, messages, tool_names) {
00429|         return Some(plan);
00430|     }
00431|     if let Some(plan) = structured_edit::plan_structured_edit_step(task, messages, tool_names) {
00432|         return Some(plan);
00433|     }
00434|     // A source-backed structured document is a read/derive/write transaction.
00435|     // It must win before the ordinary file reader, which would otherwise read
00436|     // the input correctly and then mistake that intermediate observation for
00437|     // the answer to the whole authored-artifact request.
00438|     if let Some(plan) = structured_document::plan_step(task, messages, tool_names) {
00439|         return Some(plan);
00440|     }
00441|     // A repository audit names the artifact its CLI command will produce; that
00442|     // filename is a destination, not literal content for the generic writer.
00443|     // Keep the replayable recipe ahead of literal fallback so an observed CLI
00444|     // result completes the audit instead of starting a redundant write plan.
00445|     if statement_audit::is_statement_audit_task(task) {
00446|         return Some(plan_shell_step(
00447|             messages,
00448|             tool_names,
00449|             statement_audit::command_for(task),
00450|         ));
00451|     }
00452|     // Resolve an unambiguous literal write before keyword recipes: arbitrary
00453|     // filenames/payloads may legitimately contain "issue", "report", or "learning".
00454|     // Unambiguous is the operative word: a request that also pins the target
00455|     // file's opening line has not spelled its bytes out, and content recovered
00456|     // from its prose would be written without that line (issue #1066).
00457|     // Plan 16 L2g: a request that names a source-tree file (`js/app.js … to
00458|     // typescript`) is the meta pivot's translate family, and must be claimed
00459|     // before the literal-write and obligation composers read "write it" as an
00460|     // artifact write of the goal text. The structural gate (a path token plus
00461|     // the target's canonical spelling) is cheap; the family itself is decided
00462|     // by the shared solver, whose bridge lowers it to one `translate` tool
00463|     // call — or answers with the rendered gap on a client without the tool.
00464|     if crate::meta_translate::source_tree_request(task).is_some() {
00465|         match super::conversation_recall::plan_shared_solver_step(messages, tool_names) {
00466|             super::conversation_recall::SharedSolverStep::Ready(plan) => return Some(plan),
00467|             super::conversation_recall::SharedSolverStep::NotOurs
00468|             | super::conversation_recall::SharedSolverStep::Defer => {}
00469|         }
00470|     }
00471|     // An enumerated request is planned one obligation at a time, and is not
00472|     // successfully finished until the runtime ledger has discharged every
00473|     // node with at least one execution record (issues #1099 and #1138 B5).
00474|     // Single-clause requests deliberately bypass this path and keep the
00475|     // established whole-request composer below. So does a request the shell
00476|     // executes as one command and no composer reads as an artifact write:
00477|     // "show me the working directory: then list its files" splits into clauses
00478|     // whose first half names no artifact, and the ledger reported a gap where
00479|     // the shell cascade answers the whole request (issue #907). The semantic
00480|     // resolver, not the general one: "copy" inside "a fresh repository copy"

00911| /// Run a shell command through the client-owned tool loop, then present its result.
00912| fn plan_shell_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str], command: &str) -> AgenticPlan {
00913|     let progress = Progress::scan(messages);
00914|     if progress.done(Capability::Run) {
00915|         return AgenticPlan::Final(tool_result::render(
00916|             command,
00917|             progress.run_outputs.last().map_or("", String::as_str),
00918|             crate::protocol::latest_user_request(messages)
00919|                 .as_deref()
00920|                 .unwrap_or_default(),
00921|         ));
00922|     }
00923| 
00924|     if let Some(tool) = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Run) {
00925|         return plan_one(tool, json!({ "command": command }).to_string());
00926|     }
